I've saved the Q3 results to `/work/answer.json`. Run on Q2, the same script reproduces all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest net sales | `smb`, 335,411,385원 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 247 |
| c. Category with highest net sales | `sw`, 274,938,634원 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with most refunds | u196@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 237 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 709,074원 |
| h. Growth, Aug → Sep | 18.0% |

**What I had to decide:** the DB has three quirks. I tried both readings of each against Q2, and only this combination matched every reference value:
- **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (ends in `Z`). I converted it to Korean time (UTC+9) before assigning quarters and months.
- **Who counts as one customer:** there are 300 customer IDs but only 250 distinct emails. I counted customers by email (trimmed, lowercased), not by ID.
- **Segment labels:** variants like `' consumer'` and `'Enterprise '` exist, so I trimmed spaces and lowercased them.

These choices change the answers. If I used UTC dates instead, Q3 would give a_net 330,383,476, c_net 276,000,933, f 235, g 706,548 and h 34.8%. Counting by ID instead of email would push b and f higher.

The data itself was clean: every refund and order line links to an existing record, and no refund quantity exceeds the quantity ordered.

STATUS: DONE
